To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the dual-channel IC is able to generate multiple offset outputs with an accuracy better than 3 degrees and spurious levels of better than -50dBc.

For a 2-channel X-band offset transmitter, the channel-to-channel phase difference is better than 0.5 degrees, and the spurious level is better than -65 dBc for a single-channel output, but for the two channels combined, the spurious level increases with the number of channels, to a level of -45 dBc for two channels.

(a) the channel-to-channel on-chip isolation can be improved by using a different layout and by increasing the number of metal layers; (b) the spurious level can be improved by increasing the number and the quality of the matching capacitors, and by increasing the quality of the biasing network; (c) the phase error can be improved by reducing the number of metal levels, and by reducing the number and the size of the transistors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a dual-channel offset-transmitter IC, which is suitable for both beam steering applications and DDMA applications.
the development of a dual-channel transmitter that can be used in a phased-array radar for beam steering and DDAMA.
the design of a single-chip dual-channel offset-transmitter, and the effects of the channel-to-channel coupling on the phase accuracy and spurious level.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
for beam steering applications, the dual-channel IC is a good choice, while for DDMA applications, multiple chips are preferred.
for beam steering applications, a dual-channel IC with 35dB channel-to-channel isolation is sufficient.
the proposed architecture is well suited for MIMO applications, and can be extended to the DDMA case by using multiple chips.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed architecture is a good choice for MIMO and DDMA arrays, provided that the channel-to-channel-isolation is sufficient.

we have successfully demonstrated that multiple channels can be generated on a single X-band offset-transmitter IC, with the required isolation between the channels, for both beam steering applications and for DDMA applications.
the use of a single chip for multiple offset outputs is possible, but only for applications that do not require high channel-to-channel isolation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a dual-channel X-band IC is capable of generating two offset channels with sufficient accuracy and spurious level for both MIMO and DDMA applications.
the channel-to-channel-isolation is not a limiting factor in MIMO and/or DDMA arrays, and that the main limiting factors are the spurious levels and phase accuracy.
a single chip with multiple channels may be used for beam steering, but that multiple chips should be used for DDMA.
